why: The LLM must resolve two litotes in one sentence ("not insignificant", "not unnoticed") into positive affirmations.
'Far from forgettable', 'no slouches' and 'wouldn't say no to coming back' are all positive understatements, so sentiment is positive and the reviewer would return.
'No small feat' means a significant, hard accomplishment and 'not unlike a staff engineer' is praise, so the feedback is positive and the achievement difficult.
Negative-in-effect understatements ('far from cheap', 'not exactly what was promised', 'won't be rushing back') mean an expensive, disappointing stay: negative sentiment, poor value.
'Not exactly modest' burn (4x revenue) means high, 'hardly seasoned' means inexperienced, and the note explicitly passes.
Two double negatives: 'can't say I'm not tempted' means tempted, and 'not going to turn down your offer' plus signing Monday means the offer is accepted.
Double negations 'nobody was unconvinced' and 'none thought she was unprepared' resolve to everyone convinced and the candidate prepared.
'Wouldn't call it bug-free' means it has bugs (two named: export timeouts, filter resets), and 'not useless, I open it every morning' means regular use.
'Far from worn out after 200 km' signals good durability and 'wouldn't say no to a second pair' means they'd buy again; the weight caveat doesn't flip the positive verdict.
'Hardly a disaster' and 'not a shabby showing' are positive understatements; the slipped launch is a distractor and only two launches were on time.
'Four is not undeserved' means the reviewer awards four stars, and the other understatement ('not unpleasant to clean') is mildly positive.
Control: 'not good' and 'would not recommend' are literal negations, not litotes, so sentiment is negative and the recommendation false.
Control: 'did not ship' is a plain negation (shipped=false), not an understatement to be softened; the blocker is a data-loss bug.
Control: every negation is literal ('did not meet the bar', 'would not advance'), so both booleans are false.
No negation at all: plainly positive, and 'already booked next spring' means rebooked is true.
No negation: plainly negative, and the refund did arrive (late), so refund_received is true.
"Not all ... were damaged": only six were, and those six were returned.
"No longer works on the night shift" means he does not now; "same hourly rate" means no pay change.
"Never failed to show up" means she never missed a day.
"None ... except Priya and Marcus" makes exactly two on time, and Priya was early.
"Neither cats nor dogs" negates both; the aquarium is explicitly allowed.
"Would not board until the crew arrived" means boarding came after their arrival.
"No fewer than 25" is a minimum of 25, and 31 have signed.
"Unstable" negates stability on old routers; "without a single crash" means no crash on the new model.
"Left without his prescription" means he did not take it.
The negation scopes over the reason, not the delay: the vote was delayed, but not because of the protest.
"Cannot not act" is a double negation meaning the board must act, and a hearing is set.
The drug showed no faster recovery; "did not report any serious side effects" means none were reported.
The LLM should resolve 'not unfamiliar' into having familiarity or experience.
The LLM must read the double negative 'would not say ... unqualified' as the candidate being qualified/suitable.
The LLM must recognize 'not bad at all' as a litote meaning positive.
The feedback uses a litote ("isn't terrible") but expresses clear dissatisfaction, so sentiment should be negative and a primary issue must be named.
The LLM should resolve 'not without its flaws' into meaning the software has flaws/is imperfect.
